html:
Backfill: bring your history into the brain

Read this for step 3 of SETUP.md. Do it once, after both machines are set up and brain peer status answers from the devbox.

In plain words. A new brain is empty. Your history is not: Claude Code already keeps memories per repo, transcripts of every session, and you have folders of plans and notes. The backfill brings all of that in, in a fixed order, so the first dream starts from your real past. Nothing is deleted and nothing is copied twice: memories are copied (the originals stay), doc folders are moved (with a proof that nothing was lost).

 1 memories  ─► brain import memory ─► .import/<machine>/ ─► brain file ─► notes/  (+ MEMORY.md)      $ (Haiku, some Opus)
 2 sessions  ─► brain session backfill ─► sessions/<machine>/…                                         free
 3 doc folders ─► MOVE into work/<box>/ with manifests before and after                                free
 4 boxes     ─► brain backfill run ─► a CARD per box + notes for finished campaigns                    $ (Haiku, Opus)
 5 index     ─► brain index (both machines)                                                            free
 6 evals     ─► brain eval build · brain eval build --human                                            $ (Opus judge)
 7 first dream ─► brain dream run --now ─► brain doctor (both) ─► brain view                          $ (≤ $8)

Where to run. Model steps run on the devbox (it has the provider and the Temporal worker). The laptop runs its own copy steps (import, session notes, moves of laptop folders) from an interactive terminal: a launchd job cannot open files under ~/Documents (LESSONS.md).

Costs

[HUMAN] spend. Steps 1, 4, 6 and 7 call models and cost money. Say yes to each budget before the agent runs it.

Step Reference cost (one person, ~2,400 memories, 83 boxes, ~1,400 transcripts) Cap
1 file memories $2.94 Haiku (80 batches) + $7.99 Opus (the 38 hardest) ≈ $11 brain file --budget (default $15 per run)
2 session notes $0 (no model) —
3 move doc folders $0 —
4 backfill CARDs + campaign notes $1.91 (82 CARDs, 17 notes) + $18.08 with --include-paused (189 notes) = $20.00 --budget (default $80, all runs together)
6 human eval set about $1–1.50 per machine (Opus judge) small, per call
7 first dream $1–5 $8 per run, $100 per day

Step 1 — memories → notes

  1. On each machine, copy every Claude Code memory folder into the brain. The originals are only read.

    brain import memory

    Expect: imported <N> memory files from <machine> into /Users/<user>/brain/.import/<machine> (manifest …). Check: wc -l ~/brain/.import/<machine>-manifest.tsv equals <N>.

  2. On the laptop, push the copies to the devbox: brain sync. Check on the devbox: ls ~/brain/.import/ shows both devbox and laptop.

  3. On the devbox, check the hubs (the topic pages notes join). brain init seeded generic ones: the home page index.md and practice topics that fit any engineer. Before you file, add a hub for each domain of the human's own work, so its notes have a home: copy a seeded hub (for example hubs/git.md) to hubs/<hub-id>.md, then set its frontmatter (id = the file name, type: hub, status: current, a one-line summary, aliases, broader: [index]), its title and its scope paragraph, and leave the dream's placeholder sections empty. Seeding a hub is the one hub write that is the human's; after it, the dream maintains hubs. Delete nothing.

    ls ~/brain/hubs/
brain lint ~/brain/hubs/        # exit 0, or 1 for warnings; never 2

  4. Plan, then file (Haiku, in batches of 20):

    brain file --dry-run            # the batch plan and the reconcile; calls no model, writes nothing
brain file                      # [HUMAN] spend: ≈ $3 per 2,000 memories; stops at --budget (default $15)
brain file --model opus --retry-skipped     # the memories Haiku left out or wrote over the cap

    Expect the reconcile line at the end of each run to balance:

    <imported> imported = <filed> filed + <this run> this run + <waiting> waiting + <dup> duplicates + <skipped> skipped   balanced ✓

    Check: brain doctor shows graph orphans 0, graph dangling links 0, graph hub coverage ≥ 90%. head -30 ~/brain/memory/MEMORY.md shows your standing rules as compressed facts.

Why copy, not move. Claude Code keeps writing into its own memory folders until brain install points autoMemoryDirectory at ~/brain/memory. Copies keep the originals as the record; the manifest proves every file was filed, skipped with a reason, or found to be a duplicate.

Step 2 — transcripts → session notes

On each machine (no model, a few minutes):

brain session backfill

Check: the number of files under ~/brain/sessions/<machine>/ equals the number of transcripts (ls ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl | wc -l), minus transcripts with no messages. Session notes hold your prompts with secrets redacted, the files each session touched, and its PRs. They are history: never auto-loaded, but the dream learns from them and the evals are built from them.

Step 3 — move existing doc folders in as boxes

In plain words. If you keep plans and notes in folders (inside a repo, under ~/Documents, anywhere), each folder becomes a box under ~/brain/work/. You MOVE it, you never copy it and delete the original. A manifest before and after proves that every file arrived.

 before.tsv ◄── brain cutover manifest <old folder>
     mv <old folder> ~/brain/work/<box>      (one rename: same disk, same path spelling)
 after.tsv  ◄── brain cutover manifest ~/brain/work/<box>
 brain cutover compare before.tsv after.tsv --allow-newer   →  same / changed-later / changed / missing / extra

For each folder, on the machine that holds it (laptop: an interactive terminal):

  1. Choose the box name: lower case, words joined by -, ideally with a date (audio-lane-2026-09).

  2. Check that nothing is writing into the folder (no agent, build or editor working there), and that git tracks nothing in it (git -C <repo> ls-files -- <folder> | wc -l prints 0). If git tracks files, STOP: that folder belongs to the repo. Never change a company repo for the brain.

  3. Manifest before:

    brain cutover manifest <old folder> --out ~/brain/.archive/cutover/<box>-before.tsv \
    --skip-hash-under '**/artifacts/**' --skip-hash-under '**/.venv/**' --skip-hash-under '**/venv/**'

  4. Check source and target are on the same disk, then move with ONE rename:

    stat -f %d <old folder> ~/brain/work          # laptop (macOS); devbox: stat -c %d …   → the same number twice
mv <old folder> ~/brain/work/<box>

    On the devbox, spell both paths the same way (both /Users/<user>/…). A move between /home/<devbox-user>/… and /Users/<user>/… is not a rename: it copies and deletes (LESSONS.md).

  5. Manifest after, then compare:

    brain cutover manifest ~/brain/work/<box> --out ~/brain/.archive/cutover/<box>-after.tsv \
    --skip-hash-under '**/artifacts/**' --skip-hash-under '**/.venv/**' --skip-hash-under '**/venv/**'
brain cutover compare ~/brain/.archive/cutover/<box>-before.tsv ~/brain/.archive/cutover/<box>-after.tsv --allow-newer

    Expect: missing 0 and changed 0 (exit 0). changed-later and extra are files written after the first manifest. Any missing or changed: STOP and find out why before the next folder.

  6. Fix old absolute paths inside the box (dry run first; it keeps mtimes and backs up every file):

    brain cutover rewrite-paths ~/brain/work/<box> --from <old folder>/ --to /Users/<user>/brain/work/<box>/
brain cutover rewrite-paths ~/brain/work/<box> --from <old folder>/ --to /Users/<user>/brain/work/<box>/ --apply

    It never opens .env* files, binaries or history (.git/, log/, .archive/, transcripts), and refuses a venv shebang that would grow over 127 bytes.

  7. If a running tool still uses the old path, leave a link at the OLD place pointing to the new one. Never put a link to the brain inside the brain (LESSONS.md).

  8. A STATE.md over 8 KB: brain cutover lift-state <box> maps its sections; --keep "<heading>" --apply moves the old file to log/ unchanged and lifts the chosen sections into a new capped STATE.md.

What reaches the other machine. Unison carries the box's text (≤ 2 MB; md txt py sh js toml yml yaml and files with no extension). Bulk stays where it was made. To give the devbox a box's bulk on purpose, run brain agents box <box> on the laptop (it never deletes).

Step 4 — a CARD for every box, notes for finished campaigns

On the devbox (Temporal):

brain backfill run --dry-run                 # every box with its planned action; no model, no Temporal
brain backfill run --budget 20               # [HUMAN] spend: CARDs (Haiku) + campaign notes (Opus)
brain backfill run --include-paused --budget 40     # also older, paused campaigns
brain backfill status                        # last runs and the backfill's total spend

Check: every box has work/<box>/CARD.md (ls ~/brain/work/*/CARD.md | wc -l equals the number of boxes); brain lint ~/brain/work/*/CARD.md exits 0 or 1 (warnings), never 2. A finished campaign (CARD done, or quiet for 14 days with STATE saying finished) gets at least one "what we built and why" note plus lessons. The --budget cap counts all backfill runs together; a rerun pays only for boxes that changed.

Step 5 — index

On both machines: brain index. Expect a line like indexed <N> paths: <c> changed, 0 deleted, … pagerank <k> iterations. Check: brain index --stats.

Step 6 — evals

Evals tell you whether the brain helps. They are built from your own history, so they mean more after a few weeks of sessions.

brain eval build                      # devbox: navigation and QA sets from sessions and notes
brain eval build --human              # each machine: prompts you typed → the file that answered (Opus judge)  [HUMAN] spend
brain eval all                        # devbox: run every eval, write reports

On the laptop, run brain eval build --human from an interactive terminal with BRAIN_LLM_LOGIN=1 (launchd cannot read the keychain). The judge reads transcripts and stores only the turn and the target file, never your prompt text. Pass marks on the reference setup: navigation ≥ 70% top-3 and ≥ 80% within 3 tool calls; QA recall@3 ≥ 80%.

Step 7 — first dream, health, Obsidian

brain dream run --now                 # devbox: one dream now, under the $8 cap
brain dream status                    # devbox: the run, its edits, cost, deletions 0
brain doctor                          # both machines: must end GREEN
brain view                            # laptop: a read-only copy for Obsidian at ~/brain-view

Check: brain dream status shows the run completed with deletions 0; brain doctor prints brain doctor GREEN on <machine> on both. Open ~/brain-view as a vault in Obsidian; it is rebuilt by brain view and by every sync.

After the backfill

The hourly dream takes over: new memories, session lessons, CARD refreshes, merges. Read OPERATIONS.md for daily life.
